heard: Only three people in history have died in space. In June 1971, three Soviet cosmonauts docked with Salyut-1, the world's first crewed space station. After more than three weeks of orbital experiments, their Soyuz 11 spacecraft undocked to return to Earth. Roughly 80 to 100 miles above Earth, capsule separation accidentally jarred open an air equalization valve. The cabin depressurized into space in less than one minute, with the crew wearing no pressurized spacesuits. Yet the automated ship guided itself home, surviving re-entry and touching down on parachutes in Kazakhstan. Rescuers opened the hatch expecting triumphant record breakers, but found all three cosmonauts dead in their seats. A single open valve had sealed their tragic place in history.
